title: SOC2 prep scratchpad - Isabella Chen
content:
Quick notes / brain dump for SOC2 prep (working doc)

Purpose: capture outstanding risks, control mapping gaps, owners and near-term action items for Type II readiness. Mostly notes to self and pointers for Maya + Ryan follow-up.

High-level status
- Readiness: baseline in place for CC1/CC2 (access + change mgmt), still gaps in logging retention, evidence collection automation, and onboarding checklist for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Controls in-flight: automated user provisioning (PR in review), MFA enforcement for admin roles (deploy next week), CB-logging pipeline (needs retention policy).

Unresolved / open questions (need answers before audit kickoff)
1) Log retention for Private deployments: customer-managed vs Redwood-managed? Who owns evidence? Action: sync w/ Solutions eng (Oliver) and Legal to confirm.
2) Backup verification frequency for config snapshots (Dedicated): daily vs weekly acceptable? Need input from SRE.
3) Encryption KMS key rotation evidence: do we have automated rotation logs for KMS keys used in Private offering (HSM integration)? Who is the owner for evidence extraction?
4) Change management exceptions: small infra tweaks (infra-as-code) — how do we capture approvals? Consider templated PR checklist + confluence link.

Control mapping draft notes (quick mapping to common SOC2 CC categories)
- CC2 Logical access: SSO + SCIM + RBAC enforced for hosted + dedicated. Evidence = SCIM logs, Okta admin activity reports, admin account list snapshot. (Owner: Maya)
- CC3 System operations: production deployment runbooks, canary rollout logs, incident postmortems for last 12 months. Evidence = deployment tags, runbook version history. (Owner: Ryan)
- CC4 Change management: GitHub PR approvals, CI pipeline logs, release notes for major changes. Gap = lack of preserved approver snapshot for hotfixes. Mitigation = add approver snapshot step in CI. (Owner: SRE/Release eng)
- CC6 Monitoring/logging: centralized logging retention, alerting configuration, SOC alerts (where applicable). Gap = retention policy not applied uniformly to private clusters. (Owner: Observability team + Private deployments)

Immediate action items (next 4 weeks)
- [ ] Meeting w/ Oliver (Solutions) to clarify evidence responsibilities for Private customers — by 2026-02-02 (assigned to me).
- [ ] Create Confluence template for evidence uploads + naming conventions (tag: soc2-evidence) — draft by 2026-02-09 (Maya + me).
- [ ] Add CI step to capture PR approvers and artifact hashes (Release eng) — design doc by 2026-02-14 (Ryan owner).
- [ ] Confirm KMS rotation logs retention and export process with Infra/KMS team — meeting 2026-02-06 (Ryan).
- [ ] Snapshot current list of admin accounts and export Okta reports for last 6 months — done by 2026-02-05 (Maya).

Notes to self / reminders
- When collecting evidence, prefer immutable exports (CSV/JSON) with timestamped filenames and a single S3 bucket used for audit artifacts.
- Keep a changelog file that references artifact file names + associated control mapping (helps auditor flow).
- For Private deployments, ask Legal if we need customer consent to store their exported artifacts in Redwood S3 for audit purposes.

Potential risks & mitigations
- Risk: Evidence is scattered across teams and ad-hoc folders. Mitigation: central evidence bucket + required metadata (control id, owner, date).
- Risk: Small configuration changes not captured in PR history (manual changes). Mitigation: enforce runbook + require post-change PR linking.
- Risk: Retention mismatch between hosted and private. Mitigation: document policy and make default retention configurable per deployment type.

Useful links / quick refs
- Confluence SOC2 master checklist: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/23456/SOC2+Prep
- JIRA tickets to track major gaps: SEC-4321 (logging retention), SEC-4389 (PR approver snapshot), SEC-4410 (evidence bucket setup)
- Previous audit artifacts bucket (read-only): s3://redwood-audit-artifacts/2024

Things to escalate to DRI (if not resolved in 2 weeks)
- Decision on retention policy for Private clusters (Legal + Solutions)
- Resource request for evidence ingestion script (approx 2w eng effort)

One-liners to paste into cross-team Slack threads
- "Heads up: starting SOC2 Type II prep — we need owners for KMS rotation evidence and private deployment log retention. Ping me if you own any of these."
- "Quick ask for Release eng: can we add an approver snapshot step to CI for hotfixes? Will reduce audit friction."

Scratchpad thoughts (less polished)
- Maybe we can reuse existing analytics export infra to pull Okta reports on a schedule.
- Could build a tiny lambda that packages evidence and writes a manifest file (control id, files) into the audit bucket. Low effort, high impact.
- If Legal requires customer consent for storing private artifacts, we might offer an opt-in during onboarding or provide an on-prem evidence export tool.

Next edits: refine control mappings (map to exact CC numbers and sample evidence list), create a one-page exec summary for security review, and build a checklist for Solutions engineers onboarding Private customers.

-- Isabella
